What to do when LoloBuy parcel tracking is not updating.

A fact-led checklist for reading parcel events and preparing a useful support request.

⌕

Tracking & support guide · 10 minute read

LoloBuy tracking not updating: how to check the parcel and contact support

If your LoloBuy tracking is not updating, do not begin by guessing that the parcel is lost. Start with the parcel detail page, identify the package number and waybill number, copy the latest tracking event exactly, and note when you last saw a change. Then compare the information shown in LoloBuy with the tracking channel provided for the selected route. If the status is abnormal, the address is at risk, or the carrier’s own guidance indicates that action is needed, prepare one clear support request linked to the parcel.

LoloBuy’s current public web application includes “Package Details,” “Package status,” “Tracking & logistics,” “Shipment tracking,” a waybill number field, site messages, a notice centre and a help centre. The interface also warns buyers to monitor tracking and contact the platform if abnormal updates appear. These features provide places to check and communicate, but they do not create a universal delivery schedule. Different routes, carriers, destinations and customs processes can produce different event patterns.

1. Make sure you are tracking a parcel, not a product order

A product order and an international parcel are separate records. The seller first sends an item to the warehouse; the buyer later submits stored items as a parcel for international shipping. An order number can help with a product purchase question, while a package number and waybill number are more relevant after international dispatch. Mixing the two can make a support message harder to understand.

Open the parcel record and confirm the destination country, shipping method, package status and waybill shown. If no international parcel has been submitted, there may be no international tracking to follow yet. If a parcel exists but no waybill or tracking event is displayed, record that exact condition instead of describing it broadly as “stuck.” A precise description gives support a clearer starting point.

2. Save a clean tracking snapshot

Before refreshing several websites or asking a community, capture five non-sensitive facts: the package number, shipping line, dispatch or submission date shown, latest event text and timestamp of that event. Also note whether the parcel detail page says “No tracking events yet” or displays an older event. Those are different situations and should not be reported as if they were the same.

Keep the complete waybill private when posting publicly. A partial identifier may be enough for a general discussion, but the full package and waybill numbers should go only through the platform’s appropriate support channel. Never share your address, phone number, account email, login code, payment screen or identity document in a public tracking question.

Use the event wording as written. “No update” can mean no event has ever appeared, no new event has appeared since a specific handover, or the destination carrier has not yet published a local scan. Copying the actual event prevents a support agent from having to guess which of these you mean.

3. Read tracking events as checkpoints, not promises

A tracking scan records information supplied at a stage of the route. It may describe acceptance, sorting, departure, arrival, customs processing, transfer to another carrier, a delivery attempt or delivery. It does not by itself guarantee when the next scan will appear. A gap can occur between physical movement and the next system update, especially when responsibility passes between logistics providers.

Look at the sequence, not one translated phrase in isolation. Ask three questions: where was the parcel at the last confirmed event, which organisation appears to control the next stage, and does the message request action? An event that explicitly asks for address information, customs cooperation or collection deserves more attention than a routine transit event with no action request.

Avoid importing a delivery estimate from another buyer’s screenshot. Even parcels with similar goods can use different routes, handover partners or customs processes. LoloBuy’s interface does not support one permanent shipping time for all parcels, so this guide does not invent one. The current parcel record and carrier information are more relevant than an old average.

4. Check both sides of a carrier handover

When a route uses more than one logistics provider, the same waybill may appear differently before and after handover. LoloBuy may display the consolidated event history, while a destination carrier may show local delivery activity later in the journey. Use the tracking path supplied for your parcel rather than selecting a carrier based only on a logo or a guess.

If the destination carrier recognises the number but shows no local scan, record that fact. If it does not recognise the number, confirm that you copied the waybill rather than the internal package number. Do not repeatedly submit random number formats to unrelated carrier sites; that creates confusion without improving the evidence.

5. Know when a support request is useful

Contact support when the tracking message identifies a problem, when a delivery attempt or return risk appears, when the recipient information needs urgent attention, or when the parcel has remained beyond the relevant route or carrier guidance without a new event. The LoloBuy logistics notice specifically tells buyers to watch tracking, receive parcels promptly and make contact if abnormal tracking updates appear.

This matters because the same notice says some shipping routes may not provide overseas redelivery or return service. A parcel held after a failed delivery may not be eligible for another attempt. If the event mentions an address problem, collection deadline, customs request or failed delivery, waiting for a generic estimate may be less useful than responding through the appropriate channel.

Do not create several disconnected messages for the same issue. One well-structured request linked to the parcel is easier to follow. If new evidence appears, add it to the existing conversation where possible so the history stays together.

6. Write a support message that can be acted on

LoloBuy’s message interface allows a buyer to search by order number or store name and associate goods with a conversation. Its help centre instructs users to select an order for help involving goods, shipping, returns or refunds. For a parcel-tracking issue, use the parcel or order relationship offered in the account and provide the identifiers privately.

A useful message has four parts. First, identify the parcel and route. Second, state the destination country without posting the full address in the message body unless the official form specifically requires it. Third, quote the latest tracking event and its timestamp. Fourth, ask one direct question, such as whether the parcel is awaiting a carrier handover, whether the recipient must take action, or which carrier currently holds it.

Avoid claims that the parcel is lost unless the carrier or platform has confirmed that status. “The last event shown is X and there has been no later event in the parcel page” is factual. “The package has disappeared” is a conclusion that the available evidence may not support. Calm, specific wording makes escalation easier if it becomes necessary.

7. Preserve evidence if the issue becomes a claim

A support enquiry is not automatically an insurance or compensation claim. Eligibility depends on the parcel, any protection selected, the applicable rules and the status displayed in the account. The current LoloBuy parcel interface contains a claim workflow for eligible situations and asks for a loss description and supporting evidence. That presence does not guarantee that every parcel or tracking delay qualifies.

Keep the waybill, event history and support replies. If the parcel later arrives with visible damage, preserve the outer packaging and record the condition before discarding anything. Follow the evidence instructions shown for the actual parcel. Do not manufacture screenshots, edit event timestamps or reuse evidence from another shipment; inaccurate material can undermine a legitimate request.

A practical final check

When LoloBuy tracking appears stalled, work in this order: confirm that an international parcel exists, distinguish the package number from the waybill, save the latest event, check the route-specific tracking path, identify whether any action is requested, and contact support with one concise message if the update is abnormal or outside the guidance shown for that route.

Tracking cannot promise a delivery date, but it can provide an evidence trail. Treat every scan, message and reply as part of that trail. Good tracking practice is less about refreshing constantly and more about recognising the moment when better information—or action—is needed.
